name: Al-Nabigha al-Dhubyani
bio: Ziyad ibn Mu'awiya, known as al-Nabigha and also called Abu Umama, was a poet of Dhubyan in the Hijaz. He won the favour of al-Nu'man ibn al-Mundhir, king of al-Hira, and took refuge with the Ghassanids in Syria when the king turned against him. His poems asking al-Nu'man to hear his defence became especially well known. Al-Zirikli relates that poets, among them al-Khansa', recited to him under a red leather tent at the fair of Ukaz. He places al-Nabigha's death around 604 CE.
